candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The output variable nu_t/nu is the normalized eddy viscosity, which is dimensionless as it is a ratio of eddy viscosity to kinematic viscosity. The input variables are: u_tau (wall-friction velocity scale), h (channel half-height), y (distance from the wall), and nu (kinematic viscosity). Their physical definitions and SI exponents are well-known from fluid mechanics and dimensional analysis principles. u_tau has dimensions of velocity (L T^-1), h and y have dimensions of length (L), and nu has dimensions of kinematic viscosity (L^2 T^-1). The output nu_t/nu is dimensionless (all exponents zero). This is consistent with the physical meaning of normalized eddy viscosity as a ratio of two viscosities with the same dimensions, resulting in a dimensionless quantity.

final_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The output variable nu_t/nu is the normalized eddy viscosity, which is dimensionless as it is a ratio of eddy viscosity to kinematic viscosity. The input variables are: u_tau (wall-friction velocity scale), h (channel half-height), y (distance from the wall), and nu (kinematic viscosity). Their physical definitions and SI exponents are well-known from fluid mechanics and dimensional analysis principles. u_tau has dimensions of velocity (L T^-1), h and y have dimensions of length (L), and nu has dimensions of kinematic viscosity (L^2 T^-1). The output nu_t/nu is dimensionless (all exponents zero). This is consistent with the physical meaning of normalized eddy viscosity as a ratio of two viscosities with the same dimensions, resulting in a dimensionless quantity.
